note: The awkward case. Narrative history has weak prerequisite structure — much of the order is chronology, not dependency. Kept as a fixture to watch whether the pipeline produces a corridor with no junctions.

goal.statement: Explain why the Bastille was stormed in July 1789, in terms of what had happened in the preceding months.
goal.audience: an adult who remembers no school history

capstone.prompt: A friend says the Revolution happened because the people were hungry. What is right about that, and what does it leave out?
rubric: does not reduce it to bread alone

kcs.label: France was divided into three estates, and only the third paid most taxes
misconceptions: the third estate was only the poor
the estates were about wealth rather than legal status

check.stem: A wealthy Parisian lawyer in 1789 belonged to…
options: the second estate, because he was rich
whichever estate he paid to join
distractorSource: the estates were about wealth rather than legal status
the third estate was only the poor
the estates were about wealth rather than legal status

kcs.label: The crown was bankrupt after decades of foreign war
misconceptions: the debt came from royal luxury alone
France was poor overall rather than badly financed

check.stem: The crown's debt in the 1780s came mainly from…
options: war, including backing the American revolution
distractorSource: the debt came from royal luxury alone
France was poor overall rather than badly financed
the debt came from royal luxury alone

kcs.label: The Estates-General voted by estate, so the third could always be outvoted two to one
misconceptions: the king could simply overrule the outcome

check.stem: Why did voting by estate matter so much in 1789?
options: the third estate could always be outvoted two to one
the king held the deciding vote
the second estate had no vote
distractorSource: the king could simply overrule the outcome
each delegate had one vote
each delegate had one vote

kcs.label: The third estate declared itself the National Assembly and swore not to disband
misconceptions: the Tennis Court Oath was a violent act
the Assembly was created by the king

check.stem: The Tennis Court Oath was significant because it…
options: claimed authority the king had not granted
was called by the king himself
distractorSource: the Tennis Court Oath was a violent act
the Assembly was created by the king
the Tennis Court Oath was a violent act

kcs.label: A failed harvest sent bread prices to their highest point of the century
misconceptions: the shortage was engineered by the nobility

check.stem: By July 1789 a Paris worker spent roughly what share of wages on bread?
distractorSource: hunger alone explains the Revolution
the shortage was engineered by the nobility
the shortage was engineered by the nobility

kcs.label: The Bastille was stormed for gunpowder, amid fear the king would crush the Assembly
misconceptions: it was stormed to free its prisoners
it was a spontaneous hunger riot with no political aim

check.stem: The crowd went to the Bastille chiefly for…
options: gunpowder, fearing troops would move on the Assembly
no particular reason — it was a riot
distractorSource: it was stormed to free its prisoners
it was a spontaneous hunger riot with no political aim
it was a spontaneous hunger riot with no political aim

kcs.label: Trigger and cause are different things, and the storming was a trigger
misconceptions: the event that starts something is its cause
a single explanation is enough for a revolution

check.stem: Calling the storming a trigger rather than a cause means…
options: it released pressure that had built up elsewhere
causes and triggers are the same thing
distractorSource: a single explanation is enough for a revolution
the event that starts something is its cause
the event that starts something is its cause
